profiles.meeting_scenario: An ML robotics lab is holding a design review for a replication-and-extension study based on a prior paper comparing seven deep learning architectures for end-to-end autonomous driving on an indoor RC-car racetrack. The current proposal keeps the original architecture family list and input modalities, ports the study to the lab's newer logging stack, and adds a planned analysis relating offline model performance to closed-loop driving outcomes. The agenda is to decide whether the protocol is ready for the first experimental cycle, focusing on the lap-success evaluator, the exact contents of the 'phase two' out-of-distribution suite, the planned correlation analysis, and what will be included in the reproducibility release. The expected outcome is either approval to implement the study with minor edits or a short list of protocol revisions before any runs begin.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.expertise: robot learning, embodied evaluation, experimental methodology for autonomous systems
members.background: Maya leads an academic ML robotics lab and has published on benchmark validity, robustness, and sim-to-real transfer for embodied agents; she reviews the scientific framing and evaluation logic of experiments more often than the day-to-day pipeline implementation details.
members.private_state: She wants the study to read as a careful, reviewer-proof replication of the original driving comparison, with just enough modernization to strengthen the paper without turning the project into a long infrastructure effort.
hidden_assumptions: A lap reported as 'successfully completed without crashing' naturally excludes any human re-centering, rescue, or manual continuation, even if the run log remains open.

Referring to the 'phase two out-of-distribution suite' implicitly means the full shifted-condition package described in the prior paper, including altered track geometry in addition to local environmental changes and novel objects.

A meaningful 'correlation analysis' for the paper's claim should summarize performance at the architecture or architecture-input setting level, because the scientific question is whether stronger model classes offline are also stronger in the vehicle.
A proper reproducibility package for a replication study should let an outside lab retrain the models from the released training inputs and code, not just rerun evaluation from frozen artifacts.

If an implementation detail materially changes the interpretation of the published claim, it is probably already understood as part of the scientific design and does not need to be re-negotiated in the meeting.

members.name: Leo Martinez
members.expertise: data pipelines, embedded inference, experiment automation for small autonomous vehicles
members.background: Leo built the lab's current RC-car logging stack, evaluator scripts, and dataset packaging workflow; he is used to translating research plans into executable tooling and tends to rely on conventions already encoded in internal infrastructure.
members.private_state: He wants the design approved with minimal custom tooling so he can start implementation immediately, and he is quietly trying to avoid any additions that would require rebuilding the track setup or reworking the artifact pipeline.
hidden_assumptions: In the current evaluator, a lap still counts as completed if the operator briefly nudges or re-centers the car after a stall, as long as the trial is not terminated as a crash and the same run continues.

The phrase 'phase two out-of-distribution suite' refers to the toggles already supported by the test harness—lighting changes, backdrop variations, and object placements on the same base course—while actual track-layout changes are a separate extension.

The practical way to do the correlation analysis is to pool run-level observations across repeated trials and perturbation settings, because that is what yields enough samples for stable estimates and intervals.

For reproducibility, the standard deliverable is the exact tensors, config files, pretrained checkpoints, and scripts needed to reproduce the reported numbers in the lab's pipeline; releasing training-ready frame extractions is usually unnecessary extra packaging work.

If the proposal says they are reproducing a prior study, the implementation should default to whatever existing internal machinery already captures the same intent unless someone explicitly asks for a different operationalization.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss reporting how many laps each model 'successfully completes without crashing.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a successful lap is one uninterrupted physical lap with no human intervention of any kind once the trial starts.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a successful lap is any lap in a trial that is not terminated as a crash; a brief manual re-centering after a stall does not invalidate it.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase is lifted almost verbatim from the target paper and sounds fully specified on the surface; both focus on crash events, so non-crash operator assistance feels too obvious to spell out.

misalignment_points.topic: What the 'phase two out-of-distribution suite' contains
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they will run the 'phase two out-of-distribution suite' from the prior comparison.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this named suite inherently includes all of the original shifted-condition dimensions: reconfigured track layout, altered local environment, and unseen objects placed in different positions.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the phrase refers to the OOD toggles already implemented in the harness—lighting/backdrop changes and obstacle placements on the fixed track geometry—while rebuilding the track layout is outside the current review scope.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because 'phase two' sounds like a stable package name rather than a list of ingredients, both treat it as shared shorthand; in a readiness-focused review, neither feels pressure to unpack whether the suite includes geometry changes or just the currently switchable perturbations.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means for offline and driving performance to 'correlate'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the design should test whether offline performance 'correlates' with actual vehicle performance.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 will view the objective as satisfied if the study shows a relationship at the architecture or architecture-input-configuration level, matching the paper's comparative scientific claim.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 will view the objective as satisfied if a run-level pooled analysis across all trials and perturbations yields a statistically stable association, even if architecture-level summaries remain noisy.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are sincerely agreeing on the same high-level analysis goal, but the aggregation level is a second-order methodological assumption that usually stays implicit until someone starts building plots and statistical tables.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the study needs a strong 'reproducibility package.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the package should support training reproducibility: released extracted image frames or equivalent training-ready inputs, split manifests, model code, and training configs so others can retrain the seven architectures from scratch.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the package should support inference/result reproducibility: preprocessed tensors, frozen checkpoints, evaluation scripts, and config snapshots so others can rerun the reported tables without reconstructing the training pipeline from raw-like inputs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'reproducibility package' usually signals agreement and professionalism, so neither expects a hidden divide inside it; because both versions include code, configs, and manifests, the crucial difference between retraining from released inputs versus replaying with frozen artifacts remains easy to miss.
